Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, is a figure from the Old Testament who led the Jews back from Babylon around 520 BC, governed Judah, and rebuilt the temple. He is called a son of Shealtiel several times in the Old Testament, and his descendants are traced for several generations in the Book of Chronicles. However, Matthew departs from the Old Testament record at this point.

In the TV show The Amazing Race, at the Pit Stop in Corte, teams had to follow the order of their arrival to find their next clue and a canister of goat milk. The Detour for this leg was a choice between Say Cheese or Mule, Please. In Say Cheese, teams had to make three baskets of cheese and deliver them to a storage cave to receive their next clue. In Mule, Please, teams had to properly strap a harness to a mule and deliver two milk canisters to the fromagerie.

The Binding of Isaac, as depicted in Genesis 22, is a story in which Abraham is commanded by God to sacrifice his son Isaac as a test of his faith. This story has inspired multiple pieces of music, including Marc-Antoine Charpentier's Sacrificium Abrahae.

In politics, Henry Cuellar was instrumental in the passage of the bipartisan infrastructure deal in 2021. He was one of nine Moderate Democrats who threatened to boycott a procedural vote unless House leadership first allowed a vote on President Biden's Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. The effort was successful and resulted in the passage of the $1.2 trillion infrastructure bill, which has been called a historic win for President Biden. Cuellar also supported the return of earmarks to Congress.
